step-01.script:
The angel Gabriel is sent to Nazareth and greets Mary: "Hail, full of grace." Mary is troubled, then listens. Gabriel reveals that she will conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear Jesus, Son of the Most High. Mary responds: "Behold, I am the handmaid of the Lord. Let it be done to me according to your word."

The Annunciation is the moment of Mary's free yes. God does not force grace; He invites. The Word takes flesh through humility and trust.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.

step-02.script:

Pray the Glory Be, and the Fatima prayer if desired.
Then move to the next mystery.

step-01.script:
Mary travels in haste to the hill country. Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, blesses Mary and the fruit of her womb. John leaps for joy. Mary answers with the Magnificat: "My soul magnifies the Lord." The visitation becomes both proclamation and service.

The Visitation reveals love in motion. Mary carries Jesus and immediately goes to serve Elizabeth.

step-01.script:

The Nativity shows divine glory hidden in poverty. Christ is born in simplicity and offered to the world in peace.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.

step-01.script:
Mary and Joseph present Jesus according to the Law. Simeon receives Him and praises God: "Now let your servant depart in peace." He foretells contradiction and that a sword will pierce Mary's soul. Anna also gives thanks and speaks of the child to all awaiting redemption.

In the Presentation, Jesus is offered in the Temple. Obedience, sacrifice, and prophecy meet in one holy act.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.

step-01.script:
After Passover, Jesus remains in Jerusalem without His parents knowing. After three days, Mary and Joseph find Him in the Temple among teachers, listening and asking questions. Jesus says He must be in His Father's house. He then returns with them to Nazareth in obedience.

Finding Jesus in the Temple teaches persevering search. Even holy families experience anxious waiting and renewed understanding.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.

step-01.script:
John preaches repentance and baptizes in the Jordan. Jesus comes from Nazareth and is baptized. As He rises from the water, the heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a voice declares: "You are my beloved Son; with you I am well pleased."

At the Jordan, Jesus is revealed publicly as the beloved Son, and the Trinity is made manifest.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.

step-01.script:

At Cana, Christ's first sign reveals His glory and Mary's maternal guidance: "Do whatever He tells you."

Stay with this mystery as you pray.

step-01.script:
Jesus announces: "The kingdom of God is at hand; repent and believe in the Gospel." He forgives sins, heals the sick, and restores dignity to sinners. The kingdom is not abstract; it is Christ acting with authority, mercy, and truth in human lives.

The Proclamation of the Kingdom calls every heart to conversion, faith, and mercy.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.

step-01.script:

step-01.script:
At the Last Supper, Jesus takes bread and wine and gives them as His Body and Blood: "Do this in remembrance of me." He establishes the sacrament that unites believers to His sacrifice and life. The Eucharist becomes the heart of Christian worship.

The Institution of the Eucharist gives the Church Christ's abiding presence: Body and Blood offered for the world.

step-01.script:

In Gethsemane, Jesus embraces the Father's will in agony, teaching obedience under suffering.

step-01.script:
Jesus is brought before Pilate, questioned, and rejected by the crowd. Though innocent, He is handed over and scourged. The scene shows injustice, violence, and Christ's silent endurance for the salvation of souls.

The Scourging reveals Christ's innocent suffering and the cost of human sin.

step-01.script:

The Crowning with Thorns reveals mocked kingship: Christ reigns through truth, humility, and love.

step-01.script:
Pilate yields to pressure and delivers Jesus to be crucified. Jesus carries the Cross; Simon of Cyrene is compelled to help. Women mourn as Jesus speaks to them with prophetic compassion. The road of suffering becomes the road of redemption.

On the way to Calvary, Christ carries the Cross and invites discipleship through endurance.

step-01.script:
Jesus is crucified between two criminals. He is mocked, yet forgives and promises paradise to the repentant thief. Darkness falls; then Jesus cries out, "Father, into your hands I commit my spirit," and dies. The centurion recognizes His innocence.

At Calvary, Jesus offers His life completely and opens mercy even at the hour of death.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.

step-01.script:
At dawn, the women come to the tomb and find it opened. The angel announces: "He is not here; He has risen." Jesus appears to His disciples and sends them to all nations, promising: "I am with you always, to the end of the age."

The Resurrection is Christ's victory over sin and death, foundation of Christian hope.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.

step-01.script:
After forty days of teaching, Jesus promises the Holy Spirit and ascends before the apostles. Angels declare that He will return in glory. The disciples are called from passive looking to active mission in the power of God.

The Ascension reveals Christ's lordship and sends the Church into global witness.

step-01.script:
A sound like a mighty rushing wind fills the house; tongues of fire rest on the apostles. They are filled with the Holy Spirit and speak so each listener hears in his own language. The Gospel begins to move publicly with power and clarity.

At Pentecost, the Spirit descends and gives birth to missionary courage and unity in the Church.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.

step-01.script:
The Church professes that Mary, preserved by grace and united perfectly to her Son, is taken into heavenly glory. Her Assumption is a sign of hope for the pilgrim Church and a promise of resurrection for the faithful.

The Assumption proclaims Mary's destiny in Christ: body and soul glorified with God.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.

step-01.script:
Mary, humble handmaid of the Lord, is honored as Queen because of her union with Christ the King. Her Magnificat remains the song of the redeemed, and her queenship serves the salvation of her children through prayer and intercession.

The Coronation of Mary reveals the destiny of faithful love and her maternal intercession for the Church.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.

step-02.clip_title: Meaning and intention before Our Father
step-02.script:
Mary's queenship points us toward Christ and the joy of heaven. Set your intention on persevering in faith and trusting her intercession.
Pray the Our Father.
